O.outcome_detail: Reliability and reproducibility of converting handwritten exam solutions into machine-readable text

cells.quote: Overall, it was found that MathPix with GPT-4V support was more reliable and reproducible than using only GPT-4V.
cells.note: The study compares OCR workflows in an exploratory exam-grading application; assignment and formal statistical design are not stated.

O.outcome_detail: Reliability and ability to capture grading nuances

cells.quote: The granularity of grading criteria also influences grading performance: employing a fine-grained rubric for entire problems often leads to bookkeeping errors and grading failures, while grading problems in parts is more reliable but tends to miss nuances.
cells.note: Parts-based grading is reported as more reliable, but the study also reports loss of nuance, so the overall direction is mixed.

O.outcome_detail: Reliability of grading different response formats

cells.quote: We also found that grading hand-drawn graphics, such as process diagrams, is less reliable than mathematical derivations due to the difficulty in differentiating essential details from extraneous information.
cells.note: The contrast concerns response format rather than a learner intervention; no formal assignment or statistical test is reported.

O.outcome_detail: Identification of pass versus fail decisions

cells.quote: Although the system is precise in identifying exams that meet passing criteria, exams with failing grades still require human grading.
cells.note: The study reports asymmetric performance by outcome category, not a randomized comparison with a separate grading treatment.
